title: sealed_holdout.v1
description: The sealed holdout document (plan 9.4, alpha-engine-config-I10502), published into the store at `strategy/current/holdout.json`. `seal.digest` is the content address of the canonical JSON of `payload` alone, so a payload edited without re-sealing no longer matches its own seal and `crucible.holdout.read_sealed_holdout` refuses it. The reader returns this document's METADATA only; `payload` is reachable through `crucible.holdout.unseal` alone, which refuses without a ruling reference and writes a `holdout_unseal.v1` record.

algorithm.description: The content-address function. A constant, not a choice at read time: a document naming an algorithm the reader does not implement is refused, never read approximately.

digest.description: `sha256:` + the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of `payload`.

sealed_trading_day.description: NYSE trading day the holdout was sealed on. Inside the document rather than in the key: the holdout is a standing reservation, not a per-session artifact.

sealed_by.description: Who sealed it. Free text; an unattributed seal is a seal nobody can ask about.

purpose.description: What this holdout is reserved FOR, in words. Plan 11 risk 1 is 'v2 passes its gates because its tests were written to pass'; a holdout whose purpose nobody wrote down is one somebody re-purposes.

ruling.description: The ruling that authorised SEALING this holdout, where one exists. Optional: sealing reserves data and needs no ruling; UNSEALING releases it and always does.

payload.description: The holdout itself - which sessions, instruments or folds are reserved. Its internal shape is strategy edge and is deliberately unconstrained here: this schema seals a document, it does not specify a strategy. Opaque to every reader but `crucible.holdout.unseal`.
